draft.title: Human migration
card: Modern humans (Homo sapiens) first appeared in Africa. Later groups moved out and spread across the world. Scientists trace these movements using fossils and DNA.
The age and location of fossils show when and where people lived. Early dates in a region show when people had arrived there.
Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is passed on by the mother, with no mixing from the father. It changes only slowly, by small mutations, so similar mtDNA shows a recent shared female ancestor.

Comparing mtDNA across populations builds a tree of relatedness. Together with fossil dates, it shows that the ancestors of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples reached Australia very early, at least 50,000 years ago. They are among the oldest continuing cultures.
draft.remember: Fossils show when and where people lived. mtDNA shows how closely populations are related.

a.q: Why is mitochondrial DNA useful for tracing how populations are related?
opts: It passes down the female line, so changes build up in order
It comes from both parents, so it mixes in every generation
It mutates so fast that all populations look unrelated
It is found only in fossils, so it gives their exact age
a.why: mtDNA is passed on by the mother without mixing, so small mutations build up along family lines and can be compared. Mixing from both parents would blur these lines, which is why the second option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about who passes mtDNA on.

b.q: Population X and population Y have very similar mtDNA, while population Z has many differences from both. What is the best conclusion?
opts: X and Y share a more recent female ancestor than with Z
X and Y share a more recent male ancestor than with Z
Z must have lived in the area for less time than X and Y
X and Y must have moved out of Africa before Z did
b.why: Fewer mtDNA differences mean a more recent shared ancestor, and mtDNA follows the female line. Similar mtDNA does not show the order in which groups left Africa or how long each lived in an area, so those options go beyond the evidence.
b.clue: mtDNA follows one parent only, and fewer differences mean closer links.

a.best: It passes down the female line, so changes build up in order

b.best: X and Y share a more recent female ancestor than with Z

problems.detail: The card says mtDNA 'changes only slowly'. mtDNA actually mutates faster than nuclear DNA, and this higher rate is part of why it is useful for tracing recent population splits. VCE resources describe it as having a relatively high mutation rate.

Why (a) refers to 'the second option' as wrong. In the order shown, the second option is the correct answer, so the explanation contradicts the right answer. Refer to the wrong option by its content, not its position.
Two distractors contain 'must' and the correct option does not. Absolute wording in only the wrong options lets a student rule them out without knowing the idea.

proposal.title: Human migration
card: Modern humans (Homo sapiens) first appeared in Africa. Later, groups moved out and spread across the world. Scientists trace these movements using fossils and DNA.
The age and location of fossils show when and where people lived. The earliest dates in a region show roughly when people arrived there.
Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is passed on by the mother, with no mixing from the father. It has a relatively high mutation rate, so differences build up between separated groups fairly quickly.

Fewer mtDNA differences mean a more recent shared female ancestor, but mtDNA alone does not give dates. With fossil dates, this evidence shows people reached Sahul, the landmass that joined Australia and New Guinea, at least 50,000 years ago. Their descendants include Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, part of one of the oldest continuing cultures in the world.
proposal.remember: Fossils show when and where people lived. mtDNA shows how closely groups are related.

a.q: Why is mitochondrial DNA useful for tracing how populations are related?
opts: It comes from the mother, so lineages stay unmixed
It comes from both parents, so it mixes each generation
It never mutates, so every population has the same mtDNA
It is found only in fossils, so it shows their exact age
a.why: mtDNA is passed on by the mother without mixing, so mutations build up along female lines and can be compared between groups. If it came from both parents, it would mix every generation and blur those lines.
a.clue: Think about who passes mtDNA on.

b.q: Population X and population Y have very similar mtDNA, while population Z has many differences from both. What is the best conclusion?
opts: X and Y are more closely related through the female line
X and Y are more closely related through the male line
Z has lived in the area for a shorter time than X and Y
X and Y left Africa earlier than the ancestors of Z did
b.why: Fewer mtDNA differences mean a more recent shared ancestor, and mtDNA follows the female line, not the male line. mtDNA alone does not give dates, so it cannot show how long a group lived somewhere or when it left Africa.
b.clue: mtDNA follows one parent only, and it shows relatedness, not timing.
